prior_events.content: We are seeing duplicate hold entries in the reservation queue after the delayed catalog sync runs. Can you investigate?

Investigation found that arrival-time ordering in the reservation queue reused stale hold state when the delayed catalog sync ran. The root cause is that the hold deduplication check uses item arrival time instead of canonical event time, so delayed items bypass the uniqueness window.
Recommendation: switch the deduplication check to use canonical event time from the source catalog record rather than the arrival timestamp of the sync batch.

prior_events.content: The hold queue is backing up during peak hours. What is happening?
The hold queue bottleneck traces back to the catalog sync batch size. When the nightly sync delivers more than 200 records at once, the reservation validator falls behind and holds start queuing.
The reservation notification emails are delayed again after last night's sync.

The notification delay is caused by the same catalog sync batch size issue. Large sync batches saturate the reservation validator, which blocks the downstream notification dispatcher until the backlog clears.

Observed across hold queue performance and notification delay investigations. Reducing batch size or adding validator concurrency would address both symptoms.

prior_events.content: We need to decide how to handle reservation ordering when catalog sync is delayed.

After evaluating three options (arrival-time ordering, canonical event-time ordering, and hybrid priority ordering), the recommendation is to use canonical event-time ordering. This avoids the stale-hold problem entirely and matches how the upstream catalog system sequences records.

Decision confirmed: adopt canonical event-time ordering for reservation queue processing. Migration plan: update the reservation validator to read event_time from the catalog record instead of arrival_time, then backfill existing holds.

prior_events.content: The branch checkout terminal is intermittently failing to process returns. Please look into it.

Investigation complete. The intermittent return failures trace to a race condition in the hold release pipeline. When two patrons return items within the same second, the hold release handler processes both against the same reservation snapshot, and the second release silently fails because the snapshot is already consumed.
